course.learn: Physical security protects people, buildings, devices, documents, and infrastructure from unauthorized physical access, theft, tampering, or environmental harm.
course.why: An attacker who can physically reach equipment may bypass many logical controls, so cybersecurity includes doors, barriers, surveillance, and environmental protections.
course.example: A data center uses fencing, bollards, badge access, an access-control vestibule, guards, cameras, and locked racks.
course.exam: Match the control to the threat: bollards stop vehicles; vestibules reduce tailgating; cameras detect/deter; badges control entry.

course.learn: Physical sensors detect environmental or movement conditions that may indicate intrusion or danger. Different sensors detect heat, pressure, microwave reflection, sound, motion, moisture, or other changes.
course.why: Sensors extend monitoring into the physical environment and can provide early warning before damage occurs.
course.example: An infrared motion sensor detects a person entering a restricted room after hours and triggers an alarm.
course.exam: CompTIA may ask which sensor best fits a physical condition. Focus on what each technology detects.
